title: Equivalence relations, partitions, and quotients
summary: Group elements into classes, build quotient sets, and determine which maps are independent of representatives.
abstract: Sometimes different objects should count as the same, such as integers that leave the same remainder after division by a fixed positive integer. An equivalence relation makes this idea precise by dividing a set into nonoverlapping classes. Treating each class as one element produces a quotient set. A function on the original objects then gives a function on these classes exactly when its output does not change within a class.
